verse.reading: Setting my mind unmoving in the great awareness, when will I stand rooted every day in the one awareness?
verse.nuance: பேரறிவு and ஓரறிவு, the great awareness and the one awareness, are the same thing named from two sides: its size and its singleness.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Going to far lands is desire, saying there is a family god is desire; join the light of the Brahman-knowledge we love and dance the kummi.
verse.nuance: தேசங்கள் போவது is pilgrimage or wandering; குலதெய்வம் is the lineage deity of the household. Both are put on the side of wanting.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Siva alone is the supreme guru, the preceptor; his feet alone, every day, are what one holds to; and he is the one behind Vishnu, whose epithet the run-on line begins.
verse.nuance: The unit ends in நவநீத, which belongs to the next unit (the butter-stealing, cloud-coloured Vishnu). The first line sets the theme of the whole poem: the guru is Siva, and Siva comes as guru (2168 to 2170).

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Snake who lived in the hole at the foot of the banyan, you have entered the hole at the foot of the pipal; look and look at the tip of your tail, draw in and sleep standing, and dance.
verse.nuance: The two trees and holes are cipher: tradition takes the snake as the coiled power or breath moving from one seat in the body to another, and watching the tail-tip as turning back to its root. The plain picture is only a snake changing holes and sleeping.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: Listen, son Vasimuni: in the thousand verses he gave earlier he told truly the drugs, salts, bound and melted substances and the way of gems, without a lie; in this book he will tell all the silence in order, so listen bowing.
verse.nuance: The disciple is வாசிமுனி, the breath-sage, and later வாசிநாதா; the name makes the pupil the breath itself. The earlier ஆயிரம் is an alchemical work claimed as Kakapusundar's; the verse marks the turn from alchemy to மவுனம், which the formulas of 2397 to 2403 then undo.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: So that onlookers will esteem them as eaters of kaya-kalpa, they do conjuring tricks everywhere, frauds and cheats; because they smoke ganja at set hours and eat opium straight, they roam the land like dogs, licking and sniffing.
verse.nuance: காயகாயம் is read as காயகற்பம், the body-preserving medicine of Siddha tradition; the verse says its claimants are kept going by hemp and opium instead. It is a witness to the drugs of the wandering ascetic, and treats the kaya-kalpa claim as a cover rather than denying the medicine.

finding.claim: Siddha polyherbal decoctions such as Nilavembu and Kaba Sura Kudineer have been tested in few, small COVID-19 trials, with uncertain benefit beyond standard care.

verse.reading: A root from the underworld with arsenic added, with the goblin-drug joined and white-thorn ghee poured, a red vermilion ink that terrifies the whole world: by the drug she gave I burn like a coal, my Mother.
verse.nuance: The verse lists alchemical materials, பாடாணம், வேதாளம், செந்தூரம், as the Mother's drug, and its effect is the poet's burning. Whether the burning is the heat of the awakened power or the ruin of a failed preparation is open; both readings are traditional.

finding.claim: Curcumin, though popular, is unstable, poorly absorbed and a frequent false positive in assays, and no double-blind trial has shown a clear therapeutic benefit.

verse.reading: You who count the breast that grew and rose as maya, examine in truth within yourself the body of the jiva that holds grace; if you listen to the words of the great who have gained shining knowledge, the right thought will enter your stainless heart.
verse.nuance: The first line may rebuke those who dismiss the body (or woman) as illusion, in keeping with the poet's praise of the body as Shakti; or கொங்கை may be a figure for the swelling of pride or desire. அருள்கொள் சீவர் ஆர் உடம்பு is loose: 'the body of the grace-bearing souls'.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Having drawn in, exhale within that twelve; is not the standing fire let go the sun's life? One who knows these two places is a yogi; the supreme foot that is reached is sixteen; the foot of the wind that held is twelve; drawing gently in the sixteen, holding what strained in the twelve and blowing, the risen city of eight has subsided: see.
verse.nuance: Twelve and sixteen are the Siddhars' breath numbers: the out-breath that runs twelve finger-breadths from the nose, and the moon's sixteen kalas, or an in-breath of sixteen measures held at twelve. Tradition reads பன்னிரண்டு as the sun's breath and பதினாறு as the moon's, matching 2458. புரியட்டகம், the city of eight, is the subtle body of eight parts; its subsiding is the goal of the exercise. The numbers are the whole content and their exact referents are not certain.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: It flew, when it was milked, by the way of Paychalur: what was born was breath, not female nor male. Did it renounce, did it excel, did it become pure and lofty? Not at the moment of death: Sivayam shines then too.
verse.nuance: The plain claim in line 2 is that what is born in the body's way is the breath, which has no sex. கறந்தபோது, when milked, is odd; it may be the drawing of the breath. The last line can be 'not only then' or 'not then but now'; the formula returns in 1333 with துறந்தபோது for கறந்தபோது.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
verse.nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: It is heard like the ring of anklets; the tangled path is very steep; the right-whorled conch sounds; above, look at the breath, Maiden.
verse.nuance: Anklet-sound and conch are the inner sounds (நாதம்) heard as the breath rises; tradition lists them among the ten sounds of yoga. துடுக்கம் (steepness, or roughness) is the difficulty of the channel. The stanza joins sound and breath without explaining how one leads to the other.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: While we lie on the mattress laughing with soft women, if warlike Death comes and seizes us, we too are only a dead corpse, Vaalai girl.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: Not carrying this leather bag of rice about and withering, when shall I throw off the filthy inert body and reach you?
verse.nuance: துருத்தி is a leather water-bag; filled with cooked rice it is the body, a skin full of food. சடம், the inert thing, is the body as mere matter, set against உனை, the one reached.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: Bees that love the fruit of a grove with no unripe fruit, you eat honey no bee made and sleep night and day; before you board the sailless ship and land on the far shore, can the knowledge of silence be spoken by the mouth?
verse.nuance: The images are paradoxes: a grove with no raw fruit (all ripe), honey without bees, a ship without a sail; tradition reads them as knowledge that comes without process and the body or practice that crosses without visible means. The question at the end is the firm part: மவுன ஞானம், silence-knowledge, cannot be said.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Taking a body of eight spans, what of it, my Lord? Removing the nearness of women, there is great bliss; so that the eye may see, without the body ceasing, the knowledge that gains siddhi, the siddhi of yoga ... decree: think on it.
verse.nuance: தேகம் ஒழியாமல் சித்தி பெறும் ஞானம், the knowledge that gains siddhi without the body ceasing, is the text's statement of its goal: release in the living body. போசைவிதி is an obscure word, perhaps a corruption; the sense of the last foot is lost.

finding.claim: Artemisinin, isolated from sweet wormwood after a search of traditional Chinese recipes, became a frontline malaria drug, showing traditional texts can point to real compounds.

verse.reading: Kohl-eyed wife, sons, livelihood, house: Lord of the red fire, in this world of your maya's appearances in open form, what was real day after day, as the days went by, slowly went away as a plain lie, an old tale, a dream.
verse.nuance: உருவெளித்தோற்றம், apparitions in the open, is a term for mirage-like seeing; the household is not denied but reclassified. The three words for its end, பொய், பழங்கதை, கனவு, mark a gradient from falsehood to memory to sleep.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Are the five senses, the nails that hold us, alike for all or not? Is the heavy suffering of being born from a womb alike or not? Idle men, you prattle; if you realise the truth, food, sleep and pleasure are alike for you and for me.
verse.nuance: The argument against caste from the body: the same senses, the same birth, the same needs. ஆணியான ஐம்புலன்கள் makes the senses nails that pin everyone alike. உமக்கெனக்கும் ஒக்குமே, the same for you and me, puts the poet, presumably low-born, beside the hearer.

finding.claim: Indian groups descend from a mixture of ancestral populations, and widespread intermarriage gave way to strict endogamy only about 1,900 to 4,200 years ago.

verse.reading: Not carrying this leather bag of rice about and withering, when shall I throw off the filthy inert body and reach you?
verse.nuance: துருத்தி is a leather water-bag; filled with cooked rice it is the body, a skin full of food. சடம், the inert thing, is the body as mere matter, set against உனை, the one reached.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: Water poured and kept in a vessel, when a fierce fire is set under it: did it hide in the vessel, did the fierce fire drink it, did it hide in the earth, did the long sky take it? Removing the maya of the mind, did it hide within the mind?
verse.nuance: The boiled-away water is a figure for what vanishes at death, the life, or for the world when maya is removed; the questions are the ordinary accounts (body, fire, earth, sky) and the last line is the poet's own answer, that it went into the mind. Whether மனத்துள்ளே கரந்ததோ is a question like the others or the answer is a matter of tone.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Drawing the bud up with the nose and lifting it as six, spreading the net with the tongue and building a four-square house, spreading the net with the tongue inside the four-square house, I do not see the nose and suffer entirely, my Mother.
verse.nuance: Breath drawn by the nose and the tongue turned back are the pranayama and khechari of yoga; the four-square house is read as the root or the brow. The last line admits the practice failed: he cannot find the nose, that is, the breath itself. மூவிரண்டு, two threes, may be the six centres or the breath's measures.

finding.claim: Nasal breathing entrains oscillations in olfactory and limbic brain areas and improves memory and fear recognition timed to inhalation, an effect absent with mouth breathing.

verse.reading: They bend their effort to melting the lingam, not knowing the lingam of the right kind; the tale of joining lead with gold, is it not a disgrace, girl?
verse.nuance: லிங்கம் here is the alchemists' word for cinnabar (ரசலிங்கம், சாதிலிங்கம், red sulphide of mercury), and சாதிலிங்கம் is that mineral's name; the stanza plays on the word's other sense, Siva's emblem, so a second reading has them melting idols while not knowing the true linga. வங்கம் is lead or tin, and the gold-and-lead story is the coiner's fraud.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: What if they sleep, what if they wake, what if awareness goes and withdraws? What if the five fine senses go off in every direction? For jnanis who stand filled as the body fitted within and without, there is nothing at all to think.
verse.nuance: The jnani is not asked to control sleep, waking or the senses; they are made irrelevant. நிறைந்திருந்த (filled, full) is the condition: one who is the whole has no object left for thought. The repeated இலென் (what of it?) carries the tone.

finding.claim: A microtubule-stabilising drug delayed isoflurane-induced unconsciousness in rats, consistent with but not proof of a microtubule role in consciousness.

tamil: மனமது செம்மை யானால் மந்திரஞ் செபிக்க வேண்டா;
மனமது செம்மை யானால் வாயுவை வுயர்த்த வேண்டா;
மனமது செம்மை யானால் வாசியை நிறுத்த வேண்டா;
மனமது செம்மை யானால் மந்திரஞ் செம்மை யாமே
verse.reading: If the mind is set right there is no need to recite mantra, no need to raise the vital air, no need to halt the vaasi; if the mind is set right, the mantra is itself set right.
verse.nuance: செம்மை is straightness or rightness, not mere calm. The three practices named are the Siddhars' own: japa, raising the breath along the spine, and holding the vaasi (breath as the practice). The verse does not reject them as false, it makes them unnecessary once the mind is right; the fourth line can also be read as 'the mind is the mantra', the usual way it is quoted. Whether this is a dismissal of technique or a statement of its goal is left open.

finding.claim: Slow controlled breathing is associated with greater parasympathetic activity, more alpha power and lower arousal and anxiety, though most trials are small.

verse.reading: Can he be known by the eye of flesh, and not only by the mind's eye? He abides pervading, like the flame-light of a lamp.
verse.nuance: ஓருமதோ (can it discern?) is a rhetorical question: only the inner eye sees him.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: Setting our foot on the sandal called desire, trampling the thorn-forest of ego to the root, lighting a fire in the bad quality called kaasai, we have passed beyond time and death.
verse.nuance: காசை is unclear: perhaps greed for money (காசு), perhaps a corrupt word. காலாகாலம் கடந்தோம் can mean beyond all time or beyond Kala, Death. Desire is a sandal worn under the foot: used, not renounced.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Becoming a snake at the root of ஆ, spreading its hood in the field of bliss, folding in at the root of ஊ, running and stretching out the tongue of வ: when the Siddha snake-charmer taught the mantra in which சீ lay, we cut the root of birth in ம and passed beyond maya's bonds.
verse.nuance: The syllables are the cipher: ஆ, ஊ and ம give the pranava's a, u and m, and வ and சீ the letters of சிவ in the five-letter mantra. Tradition takes the snake as the coiled power rising through the syllables. சித்தப்பிடாரனார், the Siddha snake-charmer, is the guru and also Pambatti's own name.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: The red flame of shining silence, the light that drained, and nada, crying out like tanks in the space emptied of Karuvur; the nature that spread with no fear at all; the lamp that is the Lady, trembling and crying out at the pleasures.
verse.nuance: கருவூர், the embryo town, is the womb or the body's seat (compare 1332); the space emptied of it is beyond birth. நங்கை, the Lady, is Shakti as the lamp. கயங்கள்போலக் கதறி and நயங்கள் கோவென்று are obscure; the stanza's sense beyond its nouns is not recoverable by me.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: The poet, whose love and thought go only to the quarrelsome, sinful women whose eyes run to their ears and who play with the sore at their hips, and who has not been granted the fortune of wearing the Lord's two lotus feet, describes his own body as a wilderness where the five thieves raid, a chest of urine and excrement, a casket of the two deeds, a hamlet where wind, bile and phlegm lodge, a bloody frame of filthy skin, a stinking pot, a torn rag of four cubits and nine, a garden of bitter gourd, a mound in the great cremation ground, a top spinning on the rope of desire, a ship of ceaseless disease, a changing illusion, a cage of death, a bellows for rice, a kite flying in the wind, a log that fate's Dharma cuts, a shirt the four-faced tailor stitches, a feast thrown to the pyre, a dry leaf shrivelling in the fire of lust, a tuber worms dig, a forked branch up which the shoot of sin climbs, a lump that walks as a bridegroom and ends lying as a corpse, a burden the town will not let lie, a heap of pulai flowers against the wind, frost before the morning sun, a rainbow moving in the sky, the passing shadow of a thundering cloud, a bubble on water, writing on water, a sight seen in sleep's dream, and, worse than all of these, a stain of maya; and says enough, enough, Lord, enough: show the dance of bliss while the daughter of the mountain cries 'live', take me and rule me, for that is the beauty of your grace.
verse.nuance: The names fall into kinds: the body as a container of waste, as a thing moved by what is not itself (the top on the rope of desire, the kite in the wind, the puppet of 240), as a thing already prepared for death (the log Dharma cuts, the shirt Brahma sews, the feast for the fire), and as the stock brief things, which the poet caps by saying the body is worse than a bubble or a dream because it is a மாயக் களங்கம், a stain made of maya. சதுர்முகப் பாணன், the four-faced tailor, is Brahma stitching the body; விதிவழித் தருமன் is Yama as Dharma. நான்முழத் தொன்பது பீற்றத் துண்டம் is obscure: a torn cloth four cubits long with nine (holes), or nine torn pieces of four cubits. ஊரிற் கிடக்க ஒட்டா உபாதி uses the Siddhanta word உபாதி loosely for the corpse the town hurries out. The petition at the end is brief, and the grace asked for is to be ruled (ஆண்டுகொண்டருள்), not to be released.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: They show a yoga hall and rise and float upward; they quickly learn the eight siddhis as a trick and stretch up tall; then, seized by lust, caught in the urine-bag of women, they die in this wide world like men possessed by a ghoul.
verse.nuance: அட்டசித்து வித்தை (the eight siddhis as an art) is siddhi as performance. The verse's sequence, display then lust then death, makes the showman's downfall ordinary desire, and the coarse phrase for women is the poet's contempt for the fall, not for women as such (compare 1467).

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: Yogis of silent wisdom whose inner dirt is uncut stay dirty though they live in the forest; yogis of silent wisdom who have cut the dirt within have cut off birth, though they sit among corpses.
verse.nuance: The same title, மவுன ஞான யோகிகள், is given to both kinds, so silence and the forest are not what divide them; மனத்தகத்து அழுக்கு, the dirt in the mind, is. பிணத்தடம், a place of corpses, is the cremation ground where Siddhars sat, chosen as the least pure place to make the point.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: Bowing at the place where Vishnu and Lakshmi dwell and passing beyond it, you will go on and see above the service of Rudra and Rudri, blissful girl.
verse.nuance: The gods are stations of the climb: Vishnu's centre and Rudra's centre, each with his consort, in the traditional assignment of deities to the centres. The stanza says only that one bows and passes on; where in the body these places are is tradition's gloss.

finding.claim: Nearly every cell keeps a roughly 24-hour molecular clock entrained by light, and misalignment of these clocks is linked to metabolic and mental illness.

verse.reading: The thought came to me to strew the flowers of desire; to end the strength of sin I did not get the strength of the bond, and if I had, would not the three flowers of desire stand before my eyes, my Mother?
verse.nuance: பாம வலி is read as பாப வலி, the force of sin, and பாச வலி as the strength of the bond, or of love. The three flowers of desire are unexplained; the three desires for land, gold and women is one traditional gloss. The verse may mean that love's bond, rightly placed, is the cure for lust, but the text is too compressed to be sure.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: The poet says he does not know the fruit of you who stood as the maiden stage, the ripe stage and the growing to old age, and as the stage before them.
verse.nuance: வாலை, பக்குவம், கிழம் are the stages of a life, girlhood, ripeness, age, and on this reading the Lord is the ageing itself; but வாலை is also the Siddhars' young goddess, so a coded reading has the goddess ripening into the old one. பாலை is the puzzle: the infant stage (from பாலன்), the desert tract, or a corruption; the plain reading as the first age is taken here.

finding.claim: Whether adult humans make new hippocampal neurons is disputed, with major studies reporting both near-absence and abundance.

verse.reading: Is it the mass of coarse hair, or the stretch of skin the hair grows on, or the wound packed inside the skin, or the blood that wells in the wound, or the bones standing here and there between, or the stinking marrow that drips from the bones, or the slime that oozes within, or the orderly files of crawling worms, or the heap of excrement set in water, or the ropes of tied nerves, or the disease that never leaves the body: which of these is 'I', I do not know; I searched everywhere and found it nowhere. Then, Lord of Marudur who burnt the three cities with one mountain bow, made Kama fine dust with a glance, turned the fire-mouthed poison to nectar so the gods would not die, stood beyond the two who sought you, and scorched Death for the boy's sake, half-woman, lord of Ganga, Lord of the Kaveri-girt grove where nine gems shine without the sun: because your divine grace came into my hand, I tore the veil of maya and gained the pure eye of knowledge; and having gained it I saw your greatness, and seeing it I saw myself, and saw others, and saw myself in all your states; those who do not see you are the kind that do not see themselves.
verse.nuance: The dissection is a search for the self, each part posed as a question (ஓ), and the answer is that the self is not found in the body but given by grace along with the sight of the Lord. The order of seeing matters: the Lord first, then oneself, then others, then oneself in all his states. The variant தெரியாது இன்ன (not discerning, this) for தெரிதரல் இன்ன does not change the sense.

finding.claim: The insula integrates signals from inside the body into a felt sense of bodily state, and disturbed interoception is implicated in anxiety, depression and eating disorders.

tamil: பின் இரண்டு சங்கிலிக்குள் பிணிப்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I bind the twelve-legged horse that leaps, so that it does not kick the plate, within the two chains behind?
verse.nuance: A cipher verse. The horse with twelve legs is the breath (Tirumular's ஈராறு கால் புரவி), its twelve being the twelve finger-breadths the breath travels or the twelve kalas; the two chains behind are, in the tradition, ida and pingala, or the two nostrils; சில்லம் is unexplained (a shard, a wheel, a plate). The plain sense is a wild horse tethered; the cipher makes it the breath held.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: The body is impermanent; in it, infatuation is not contained by desire alone; if one stays alone, that enjoyment, standing as oneself alone, is Siva-yoga.
verse.nuance: தனித்திருந்தால், staying alone, is both solitude and the standing-as-one (தானாகி நிற்பது) that the stanza calls Siva-yoga; the enjoyment (போகம்) desire sought is redefined as the yogi's. The second line is compressed; ஆசையும் ஒன்றால் may mean that desire, being one thing, does not contain the infatuation it breeds.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: His own command is the only command upon himself; he has no other law over him; and for all time (2196) his fame does not change.
verse.nuance: The guru's autonomy is the claim: no scripture, sect or god rules him, which the attacks of 2181 and 2221 to 2233 presuppose.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: The pedestal of the linga in the body, the three letters of the unspoken mantra, the conch and the discus, all the sky; the yogis who have taken their share there, the five supreme gates and the lion-roar sound: nothing is other than Sivayam.
verse.nuance: The gloss gives அசவை as the ajapa mantra, the unrecited syllables of the breath (in tradition ஹம்ஸ or சோகம்), here counted as three letters. Conch and discus are Vishnu's, so the stanza claims the Vaishnava emblems for Sivayam too. பரம வாசல் அஞ்சு, the five supreme gates, is not fixed, perhaps the five senses or five centres. Near-repeat of 1138.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: I will tell you one great medicine to cut off both birth and death, so hear it eagerly: know the way to open with the key the lock of the mind and the door of thought, and dance.
verse.nuance: The great medicine (பெருமருந்து) is not a drug but a knowing; the lock and door are the mind's, so the release is an opening of the mind rather than an escape from the body.

finding.claim: A single 25 mg dose of psilocybin with psychological support reduced treatment-resistant depression scores at three weeks more than 1 mg, with adverse events in both arms.
